_comment: Core settings seeded on every update_database run. Plugin-owned settings live in the plugin's plugin.json. See specs/declarative_plugin_settings.md for the scope principle. Values are always strings (use '0'/'1' for booleans, '42' for numbers).

settings.name: backup_recovery_public_key
settings.label: Backup recovery public key
settings.helptext: The public half of the recovery keypair whose private half you keep in your password manager. Every backup this site makes seals a copy of its encryption key to this value, so that one private key opens every backup forever. Set it through the Backup recovery panel, which generates the keypair, takes the public half, and then has you open a challenge to prove the private half works. That proof is the whole point: a mistyped key would seal happily while producing archives nobody can ever open. Encrypted backups refuse to run until it is proven.

settings.name: backup_recovery_public_key_proven_fpr
settings.helptext: Fingerprint of the recovery public key whose private half has been demonstrated. Written by BackupRecoveryKey after the possession ceremony; its presence is what makes the recovery key honored.

settings.name: backup_target_id
settings.label: Backup target
settings.helptext: Scheduled backups are uploaded here. With none chosen the backup task skips, since there would be nowhere to put the result.

settings.name: backup_type
settings.label: What to back up

options.project: Whole site (files, database, web server config)

settings.helptext: The whole site is the restorable unit: files without their database, or the reverse, will not bring a site back on their own. Database only is for a site whose files come from somewhere else, such as a rebuild-from-source deployment.

settings.name: backup_mode
settings.label: How backups are taken

options.chain: Incremental — a periodic full, then only what changed

settings.helptext: Incremental uploads only the files that changed since the last run, and a restore replays deletions as well as changes, so any day restores to exactly how the site looked. The database is dumped in full every run either way — it is the small part, and a partly-applied database is not something anyone wants to restore.

settings.name: backup_full_interval_days
settings.label: Days before a fresh full backup
settings.helptext: How long one chain runs before the next backup starts a new one with a full. Shorter chains cost more storage and restore faster; longer chains cost less and mean more archives to apply. Only applies to incremental backups.

settings.name: backup_retention_count
settings.label: Restore points to keep offsite
settings.helptext: How many backups to keep in the bucket. Older ones are deleted oldest-first, and only ever after a newer backup has been confirmed uploaded — a run that failed never causes an older backup to be removed.

settings.name: backup_output_dir
settings.label: Where backups are written on this machine
settings.helptext: The working directory backups are built in before upload, and the one the local sweep prunes. Leave it blank and backups are written to the site's own backups folder, beside your logs and uploads — that works everywhere and is already left out of published archives. Set an absolute path only to put them somewhere else, such as a larger disk.

settings.name: backup_exclude
settings.label: Also leave out of backups
settings.helptext: Comma-separated directory names, on top of the ones always skipped (backups, vendor, node_modules, .git, logs, cache, tmp, sessions). For build output and regenerable caches — anything large that a restore would rebuild anyway. Names only, not paths — and a name matches a directory of that name at any depth in the tree.

settings.name: backup_local_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep backups on this machine
settings.helptext: Local copies are a convenience, not the archive. This also sweeps the auto_pre_* snapshots a restore leaves behind, which are the same size as a full backup and were never cleaned up by anything. 0 means never delete local files.

settings.name: backup_delete_local_after_upload
settings.label: Delete the local copy once uploaded

options.0: No — keep it until it ages out

settings.helptext: For machines with little disk. Leaving it off means a restore can use the local copy without a download.

settings.name: backup_path_slug
settings.label: Name this site files backups under
settings.helptext: The folder inside the bucket that holds this site's backups. Blank uses the project directory name, which is also what a fleet control plane would call this site — so leaving it blank keeps one pile rather than starting a second beside the first. Letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores only.

settings.name: activation_required_login
settings.label: Require email activation to sign in

settings.name: api_min_client_versions
settings.helptext: JSON map of client_app header value to minimum allowed client_version (semver). Clients below their minimum receive HTTP 426 UpgradeRequired on every API request. Empty map disables enforcement.
settings.label: Minimum client versions (JSON)

settings.name: api_require_https
settings.label: Require HTTPS for API requests
settings.helptext: Turn off for local development only.

settings.name: api_session_key_lifetime_days
settings.helptext: Days until an API session key minted by /api/v1/auth/login expires (apk_expires_time). Existing keys keep the expiry they were minted with.
settings.label: Session key lifetime (days)

settings.name: idempotency_key_retention_hours
settings.helptext: How long a stored idempotency key is honoured for replay. Needs only to outlive the retry window a client would use. 0 keeps them indefinitely.
settings.label: Idempotency key retention (hours)

settings.name: app_bridge_key_check_seconds
settings.helptext: How often (seconds) an app-context web session re-verifies that its originating API session key is still live. 0 checks on every request. Lower values make key revocation propagate to app webviews faster at the cost of a key lookup per interval.
settings.label: App bridge key check interval (seconds)

settings.name: app_navigation
settings.helptext: JSON map of client_app to the ordered menu slugs pinned to that app's tab bar (GET /api/v1/app/navigation). The default key applies to apps without their own entry; all other entries land in the app's More list.
settings.label: App navigation (JSON)

settings.name: dns_move_pending
settings.helptext: JSON state of an in-flight DNS relocation (domain, target, nameservers, copied records). Written when the guided move seeds the destination zone; cleared when the domain's nameservers reach the target or the operator cancels. Lets the wizard's dns stage keep showing the handover across reloads while delegation propagates.

settings.name: dns_default_provider
settings.helptext: The DNS host the publish box leads with. A provider NAME, never a secret — the key of a driver in includes/dns/drivers/ (linode, cloudflare, route53, …). Any other driver stays available behind the box's "use another provider" link.
settings.label: Default DNS provider

settings.name: enable_hsts
settings.label: Send Strict-Transport-Security
settings.helptext: Tells browsers to reach this domain over HTTPS only, for a year. Leave off where plain HTTP is still needed.

settings.name: newsletter_active
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: oauth_microsoft_tenant
settings.label: Microsoft tenant
settings.helptext: common accepts any Microsoft account. Name a directory id to restrict sign-in to one tenant.

settings.name: passkeys_enabled
settings.helptext: Emergency kill switch for passkey sign-in, enrollment, and PRF-based secret derivation. On by default — vault setup and protected mailboxes depend on it. Turn off only to disable all passkey operations deployment-wide.
settings.label: Passkeys enabled

settings.name: show_admin_bar
settings.label: Show the admin bar
settings.helptext: The bar shown to signed-in admins on public pages.

settings.name: signal_bus_debug
settings.helptext: When on, the signal bus logs every dispatch (signal name + JSON payload) to the error log and flags any non-JSON-serializable payload value. Debug only; leave off in production.
settings.label: Signal bus debug logging

settings.name: tier_upgrade_url
settings.label: Where the upgrade prompt links to
settings.helptext: Optional. A path, e.g. /pricing.

settings.name: vault_deferred_work_slice_seconds
settings.helptext: How long one batch of deferred work may run. Deferred work is work that can only happen while a user has their vault unlocked — parsing encrypted mail, and the AI email features on an encrypted domain. It runs in its own request, not on the keep-alive ping, so a slow model can never stall the ping that holds the window open.
settings.label: Deferred work batch length (seconds)

settings.name: vault_unlock_idle_minutes
settings.helptext: Sealed Vault unlock window idle timeout, in minutes. One unlock opens every server-custody consumer (mail, chat); the window is extended on activity and wiped on close.
settings.label: Lock the vault after idle (minutes)

settings.name: debug
settings.label: Debug mode
settings.helptext: Site-wide, not payments-only: it drives component render tracing, FormWriter debug output, and the Stripe and Google Play helpers' test behaviour. Leave off in production.

settings.name: email_test_mode
settings.label: Redirect all mail to one address
settings.helptext: Every outgoing message — To, Cc and Bcc — is delivered only to the address below, with the original recipients named in the subject line. The send path runs for real; no real person is written to. With no address configured, sends are suppressed and logged rather than delivered. The safety switch for a staging or test copy of a site.

settings.name: email_test_send_last_success
settings.helptext: UTC timestamp of the last successful test send. Written by the setup wizard's test button; read by the sending-email setup step.

settings.name: email_validation_mx_check
settings.label: Check that an address domain accepts mail
settings.helptext: On rejects addresses whose domain has no mail server. Off skips the DNS lookup, which suits bulk imports and internal domains.

settings.name: force_https
settings.helptext: DEAD. Superseded by protocol_mode, which is what the platform reads. Only migrations/protocol_mode_migration.php still names it. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: social_settings_active
settings.label: Edit social links
settings.helptext: Reveals the link fields below. It is a disclosure for this page only — a theme shows whichever links are filled in regardless of this switch.

settings.name: tier_gate_hide_from_listings
settings.label: Hide gated content from listings
settings.helptext: Applies to members who lack the tier. RSS always hides gated items regardless.

settings.name: tier_gate_preview_length
settings.label: Preview length (characters)
settings.helptext: Body text shown before the paywall. 0 shows no preview.

settings.name: totp_remember_device_days
settings.label: Trusted device duration (days)
settings.helptext: How long the sign-in interstitial's Trust-this-device choice skips the second factor on that device. 0 never offers it.

settings.name: totp_require_admins
settings.label: Require 2FA for admin accounts
settings.helptext: Admins at permission 5 and above without 2FA are sent to /profile/security until they enrol.

settings.name: totp_issuer_name
settings.label: Name shown in the authenticator app
settings.helptext: Optional. Falls back to the site name.

settings.name: use_blog_as_homepage
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. The homepage override is alternate_homepage. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: api_auth_rate_limit_requests
settings.label: Max failed sign-in attempts per window
settings.helptext: Counted per IP.

settings.name: api_auth_rate_limit_window
settings.label: Failed sign-in window (seconds)
settings.helptext: 900 is fifteen minutes.

settings.name: api_device_link_rate_limit_requests
settings.label: Max device-link requests per window
settings.helptext: Counted per IP. A computer being linked polls every few seconds for up to ten minutes, so this is deliberately roomier than the sign-in limit.

settings.name: api_device_link_rate_limit_window
settings.label: Device-link window (seconds)
settings.helptext: 3600 is one hour.

settings.name: api_rate_limit_requests
settings.label: Max API requests per window
settings.helptext: Counted per IP.

settings.name: api_rate_limit_window
settings.label: API rate limit window (seconds)
settings.helptext: 3600 is one hour.

settings.name: max_entity_photos
settings.label: Photo limit per entity (JSON)
settings.helptext: How many photos each kind of record may carry, as a JSON object. Example: {"user": 6}.

settings.name: calendar_email_log_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep the calendar email log
settings.helptext: The send ledger for calendar reminder and summary emails. The daily retention sweep deletes anything older. 0 keeps them indefinitely.

settings.name: request_log_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep request logs
settings.helptext: The daily retention sweep deletes anything older. 0 keeps them indefinitely.

settings.name: error_log_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep error records
settings.helptext: The daily retention sweep deletes anything older. 0 keeps them indefinitely.

settings.name: notification_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep read notifications
settings.helptext: Only notifications a member has already read are removed; unread ones are kept however old. 0 keeps everything indefinitely.

settings.name: allowed_upload_extensions
settings.label: Allowed upload extensions
settings.helptext: Comma separated, no dots. An extension absent from this list is refused on upload.

settings.name: anti_spam_answer
settings.label: Anti-spam word
settings.helptext: Leave blank for none.

settings.name: anti_spam_answer_comments
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. Comment spam control is use_captcha_comments. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: cloud_storage_draining
settings.helptext: Written by the cloud storage page. Set while files are being moved back off the public bucket.

settings.name: cloud_storage_enabled
settings.helptext: Written by the cloud storage page once a bucket passes its connection test, and by the pause control. Never set by hand — turning it on without a working bucket breaks uploads.

settings.name: cloud_storage_endpoint
settings.label: Endpoint hostname
settings.helptext: For example s3.us-west-002.backblazeb2.com or s3.amazonaws.com. With or without https://.

settings.name: cloud_storage_private_bucket
settings.helptext: A second bucket on the same account, sharing the endpoint, region and keys above. On save it is tested to confirm anonymous reads are denied before anything is stored there. Leave empty for no private store.
settings.label: Private bucket name

settings.name: cloud_storage_private_draining
settings.helptext: Written by the cloud storage page. Set while files are being moved back off the private bucket.

settings.name: cloud_storage_private_enabled
settings.helptext: Written by the cloud storage page once the private bucket is confirmed to deny anonymous reads.

settings.name: cloud_storage_public_base_url
settings.label: Public base URL
settings.helptext: Leave empty to derive it from the endpoint and bucket. Set it when a CDN fronts the bucket, e.g. https://cdn.example.com.

settings.name: cloud_storage_region
settings.label: Region
settings.helptext: For example us-east-1 or us-west-002. Auto-fills from the endpoint where the endpoint says.

settings.name: cloud_storage_secret_key
settings.label: Secret key
settings.helptext: Rotate it with the bucket provider if you suspect it has been exposed.

settings.name: cookie_consent_mode
settings.label: Cookie consent mode
settings.helptext: Auto picks by visitor location. GDPR asks before setting cookies; CCPA offers an opt-out.

settings.name: email_fallback_service
settings.label: Fallback email service
settings.helptext: Used when the primary service fails.

settings._comment: Empty by default, and deliberately so. A new site has no mail credentials of any kind, so any preselected provider would be configured-but-useless: the site would look set up, and a failed send would report that provider's authentication error rather than the truth, which is that nobody has chosen a provider yet. Empty is representable here and EmailSender reports it as unconfigured. Existing sites carry a value in stg_settings and are unaffected, since a declared default only applies when the row is absent.
settings.name: email_service
settings.label: Primary email service

settings.name: mailing_list_provider
settings.label: Provider
settings.helptext: Service subscriptions are synced to.

settings.name: mailchimp_default_merge_fields
settings.label: Default merge fields (JSON)
settings.helptext: Merge tags applied to every subscribe call. Example: {"MMERGE3":"Yes"}. Blank or {} for none.

settings.name: form_style
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. Form appearance comes from the .jy-ui kit. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: protocol_mode
settings.label: Protocol mode
settings.helptext: Controls the protocol on generated URLs and whether plain HTTP is redirected.

settings.name: protocol_observed_scheme
settings.label: Observed protocol
settings.helptext: Recorded automatically from real web requests when Protocol mode is Auto. Cron and CLI have no request to detect from, so they use this to build correct links. Not normally edited by hand; setting Protocol mode explicitly overrides it.

settings.name: standard_error
settings.default: Sorry, that operation caused an error.
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. Error copy comes from the page that raises it. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: tracking
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. tracking_code is emitted whenever it is set, without consulting a mode. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: composerAutoLoad
settings.label: Composer path
settings.helptext: Directory holding autoload.php, e.g. ../vendor/. The directory, not the file.

settings.name: member_area_app_chrome
settings.label: Member area uses app chrome
settings.helptext: Render member pages (/profile, /drive) with the platform app layout instead of the public theme, so calendar, mail, and drive get full-width chrome. The public site keeps the theme either way.

settings.name: upload_web_dir
settings.label: Upload web directory
settings.helptext: Web-visible path uploads are served from, relative to the site root. Usually just uploads.

settings.name: alternate_homepage
settings.label: Page to use as the homepage
settings.helptext: Optional. Leave blank to use the built-in homepage.

settings.name: alternate_loggedin_homepage
settings.label: Page to use as the signed-in homepage
settings.helptext: Optional. A path, e.g. /dashboard.

settings.name: api_allowed_origins
settings.label: Allowed CORS origins
settings.helptext: Comma separated, e.g. https://example.com,https://app.example.com. Blank disables CORS.

settings.name: blog_subdirectory
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. The setting was retired in migration 32; only a comment in migrations.php still names it. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: contact_email
settings.label: Contact email
settings.helptext: Public contact address. Shown by themes that carry a contact block.

settings.name: cookie_privacy_policy_link
settings.label: Privacy policy URL
settings.helptext: Path to the privacy policy page, shown in the consent banner.

settings.name: defaultreplyto
settings.label: Default Reply-To
settings.helptext: Applied to system mail that sets no Reply-To of its own.

settings.name: joinery_direct_enabled
settings.label: Deliver Joinery to Joinery directly
settings.helptext: Enable Joinery to Joinery encrypted messaging.

settings.name: joinery_direct_max_parts
settings.label: Most pieces in one delivery
settings.helptext: A delivery arrives as separate pieces — the message text, the formatted version, and one per attachment — so a big attachment never has to be squeezed through a single request. This is the most pieces one delivery may declare. A sender that declares more is turned away before any content crosses the wire, and its message arrives as ordinary email instead.

settings.name: joinery_direct_max_part_bytes
settings.label: Largest single piece (bytes)
settings.helptext: The biggest one attachment or body may be. This is what actually bounds memory, because a piece is sealed in one go: nothing larger than this is ever held at once, no matter how large the whole message is.

settings.name: joinery_direct_max_total_bytes
settings.label: Largest whole delivery (bytes)
settings.helptext: The biggest a whole message may be, counting every piece. Checked before any content is sent, so an oversized message costs the sender a refusal rather than the bandwidth.

settings.name: joinery_direct_spool_domain_cap_bytes
settings.label: Held-mail limit per domain (bytes)
settings.helptext: On a Private or Fortress domain a direct message is accepted and held sealed until its recipient next unlocks, because only they can say whether the sender is welcome. This caps how much can be waiting at once for the whole domain. Past it, further deliveries are refused and the sender's message comes by ordinary email instead — nothing is lost.

settings.name: joinery_direct_spool_address_cap_bytes
settings.label: Held-mail limit per address (bytes)
settings.helptext: The same limit, per individual address, so one flooded recipient cannot use up the whole domain's allowance.

settings.name: joinery_direct_spool_retention_days
settings.label: Discard held mail after (days)
settings.helptext: How long a held delivery waits for an unlock that never comes before it is discarded. 0 keeps it indefinitely.

settings.name: joinery_direct_preflight_limit
settings.label: Deliveries accepted per sending instance
settings.helptext: How many delivery attempts one other instance may make inside the window below, counted against the identity its signature proves — so one instance cannot flood this box no matter which of your addresses it aims at.

settings.name: joinery_direct_preflight_window
settings.label: Rate window (seconds)
settings.helptext: The rolling window the limit above is counted over.

settings.name: joinery_direct_session_ttl
settings.label: Time to finish a delivery (seconds)
settings.helptext: Once a delivery is accepted the sender has this long to finish sending its pieces. After that the part-finished delivery is thrown away and the sender has to start again — which it does automatically.

settings.name: joinery_direct_connect_timeout
settings.label: Connect timeout (seconds)
settings.helptext: How long to wait for another instance to answer before giving up and sending the message as ordinary email.

settings.name: joinery_direct_request_timeout
settings.label: Request timeout (seconds)
settings.helptext: How long a single delivery request may take before it is abandoned in favour of ordinary email.

settings.name: joinery_direct_decoy_secret
settings.helptext: The per-domain secret behind the stand-in key a Private or Fortress box hands back for an address that does not exist, so that answering a delivery attempt never reveals which of your addresses are real. Minted on first use and never displayed.

remote.message: Must start with / and the file must exist

settings.name: mailchimp_api_key
settings.label: MailChimp API key
settings.helptext: Ends with a datacentre suffix, e.g. -us21.

settings.name: mailchimp_list_id
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. A list is chosen per mailing list, in mlt_provider_list_id. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: mailjet_api_key
settings.label: Mailjet API key
settings.helptext: Public half of the pair, from Mailjet under Account, API Keys.

settings.name: mailjet_api_secret
settings.label: Mailjet API secret
settings.helptext: Secret half of the pair. Mailjet shows it once, at issue.

settings.name: mailjet_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only. Mailjet checks the From at send time.

help_modal.title: Get a Mailgun API key

steps.text: Create a Mailgun account, or sign in.
Open your account's API keys page and create a new key.

steps: Copy the key — Mailgun shows it only once — and paste it here. Joinery will take care of everything automatically.
help_modal.caution: Not the webhook signing key or the public validation key that live nearby — sending needs a Mailgun API key.

settings.name: mailgun_domain
settings.label: Mailgun domain
settings.helptext: For example mg.example.com.

settings.name: mailgun_eu_api_link
settings.label: Mailgun EU API URL
settings.helptext: EU-region accounts only, e.g. https://api.eu.mailgun.net.

settings.name: mailgun_webhook_signing_key
settings.label: Mailgun Webhook Signing Key
settings.helptext: HTTP Webhook Signing Key from your Mailgun dashboard (separate from the API key).

settings.name: brevo_api_key
settings.label: Brevo API key
settings.helptext: v3 API key from Brevo, under SMTP and API. Starts with xkeysib-.

settings.name: brevo_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only. Brevo checks the From at send time against senders verified in Brevo.

settings.name: postmark_message_stream
settings.label: Message stream
settings.helptext: outbound is the default transactional stream. Broadcast mail uses the broadcast stream id on the server.

settings.name: postmark_server_token
settings.label: Postmark server token
settings.helptext: A Server token, found under Servers, then API Tokens. Not an Account token.

settings.name: postmark_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only. Postmark checks the From against your sender signatures at send time.

settings.name: resend_api_key
settings.label: Resend API key
settings.helptext: From resend.com under API Keys. Starts with re_.

settings.name: resend_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only. The domain must be DNS-verified in Resend.

settings.name: sendgrid_inbound_secret
settings.label: Inbound Parse Shared Secret
settings.helptext: SendGrid Inbound Parse does not sign its POSTs. Set a secret here and append it to the Destination URL as ?secret=… so only SendGrid can deliver mail. Inbound is rejected while this is blank.

settings.name: sendgrid_inbound_spam_threshold
settings.label: Inbound spam score threshold
settings.helptext: When content spam filtering is on, an inbound spam_score at or above this value is judged spam. Default 5.0; lower is stricter.

settings.name: sendgrid_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only, e.g. mail.example.com. Must be verified in SendGrid.

settings.name: ses_access_key_id
settings.label: AWS access key id
settings.helptext: Leave blank to use the instance IAM role on EC2, ECS or Lambda.

settings.name: ses_configuration_set
settings.label: Configuration set
settings.helptext: Optional. An SES configuration set for engagement tracking, event publishing or IP pool selection.

settings.name: ses_secret_access_key
settings.label: AWS secret access key
settings.helptext: Leave blank when using IAM role credentials.

settings.name: ses_verified_domain
settings.label: Verified sender domain
settings.helptext: For reference only. Must be verified in this AWS region.

settings.name: tracking_code
settings.label: Tracking code
settings.helptext: Analytics snippet injected into every public page. Subject to cookie consent when consent is on.

settings.name: upgrade_location
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader. utils/upgrade.php reads a key of that name out of the publish response, not out of settings. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: upgrade_source
settings.label: Upgrade source
settings.helptext: The deployment this site pulls upgrades from.

settings.name: root_node
settings.helptext: Domain of the deployment where this code is written and from which themes and plugins are published — the origin of the whole estate. Empty on every site that consumes releases, which is nearly all of them, and that is the ordinary case — empty reads as not-the-origin and changes nothing. A site whose own webDir matches this value serves its own catalog instead of fetching one, sees every extension whatever audience it declares, refuses to upgrade itself from a downstream copy of its own code, and always may mint a release number. Named by domain rather than a flag so a clone or a restored backup carries it unchanged and still reads as not-the-origin.

settings.name: active_theme_plugin
settings.label: Active theme plugin
settings.helptext: Which plugin provides the user interface. Used when the active theme is plugin.

settings.name: email_test_recipient
settings.label: Address that receives the redirected mail

settings.name: nickname_display_as
settings.label: Nickname display as
settings.helptext: Leave blank to turn nicknames off.

settings.name: preview_image
settings.label: Preview image
settings.helptext: Shown when the site is shared on Facebook, Google and similar.

settings.name: preview_image_increment
settings.helptext: Cache-buster for the preview image. Bumped by the settings save when the image changes; read when the tag is built.

settings.name: site_template
settings.label: Site location
settings.helptext: The folder under the base path this deployment runs from.

settings.name: jy_color_bg
settings.label: Page background
settings.helptext: Overall page background behind cards.

settings.name: jy_color_primary
settings.label: Primary / button colour
settings.helptext: Buttons, checkboxes, links, focus rings.

settings.name: jy_color_primary_hover
settings.label: Primary hover colour
settings.helptext: Button hover state. Typically a darker shade of the primary colour.

settings.name: jy_color_primary_text
settings.label: Primary button text colour
settings.helptext: Text on filled primary buttons. Usually white; change it for light primaries.

settings.name: jy_color_surface
settings.label: Surface / card background
settings.helptext: Background of auth cards, panels and table rows. White removes the grey tint.

settings.name: drive_active
settings.helptext: Master switch for the member Drive (/drive). Off by default; enable per instance.
settings.label: Drive module active

settings.name: drive_trash_retention_days
settings.helptext: A file or folder in Drive trash is permanently deleted this many days after it was trashed. 0 keeps trash indefinitely.
settings.label: Trash retention (days)

settings.name: drive_change_feed_retention_days
settings.helptext: How long the change feed sync clients replay is kept. Must comfortably exceed the longest a client might stay offline. 0 keeps it indefinitely.
settings.label: Change feed retention (days)

settings.name: drive_stale_upload_retention_hours
settings.helptext: An upload that stops partway is discarded after this many idle hours, along with its scratch file. 0 keeps them indefinitely.
settings.label: Abandoned upload retention (hours)

settings.name: drive_device_link_grace_minutes
settings.helptext: How long a finished device-linking code is kept after it expires or is answered. 0 keeps them indefinitely.
settings.label: Device link retention (minutes)

settings.name: drive_max_folder_depth
settings.helptext: Maximum nesting depth for Drive folders.
settings.label: Maximum folder depth

settings.name: drive_upload_chunk_bytes
settings.helptext: Chunk size (bytes) the Drive resumable upload protocol requests. Default 8 MiB.
settings.label: Upload chunk size (bytes)

settings.name: api_agent_rate_limit_requests
settings.helptext: Max agent-channel requests per window per IP (own bucket, not the general API limit). A node agent polls for work on a seconds cadence, so this is sized for machine traffic.
settings.label: Max agent channel requests per window

settings.name: api_agent_rate_limit_window
settings.helptext: Window (seconds) for the agent channel rate limit.
settings.label: Agent channel rate limit window (seconds)

settings.name: agent_join_request
settings.helptext: JSON handoff from the Management Node admin page to this machine's root agent: {url, requested_time}. The web tier writes it when the admin asks to connect to a management node; the agent consumes it, performs the node-initiated join (no secret — the agent generates its own keypair), and clears it. Never holds a credential.

settings.name: agent_join_state
settings.helptext: JSON status the root agent writes back while joining a management node: {status, url, fingerprint, node_id, node_slug, error, updated_time}. The Management Node admin page renders it — including the key fingerprint the operator compares against the management node's approval screen.

settings.name: api_upload_rate_limit_requests
settings.helptext: Max Drive chunk-upload requests per window per IP (own bucket, not the general API limit).
settings.label: Max uploads per window

settings.name: api_upload_rate_limit_window
settings.helptext: Window (seconds) for the Drive chunk-upload rate limit.
settings.label: Upload rate limit window (seconds)

settings.name: webDir
settings.label: Web Domain

messages.pattern: Enter the domain only — no http:// or https://, and no slashes.

settings.helptext: The site's domain, e.g. example.com. Everything that builds an absolute URL reads this.

settings.name: baseDir
settings.label: Base path
settings.helptext: Filesystem path to the deployment root. Overridden when Globalvars_site.php hardcodes it, in which case the field is shown read-only.

settings.name: node_dir
settings.label: Node Path
settings.helptext: Path to the node install used for asset builds, e.g. /var/www/html/mysite/node. Empty when the deployment has none.

settings.name: apache_error_log
settings.label: Apache Error Log Path
settings.helptext: Read by the admin log viewer. Must be a readable file — an unreadable path makes the settings page refuse every save.

settings.name: siteDir
settings.helptext: Auto-calculated from baseDir by Globalvars. Shown read-only on the settings page; never edited directly.

settings.name: upload_dir
settings.helptext: Auto-calculated from baseDir by Globalvars. Shown read-only on the settings page; never edited directly.

settings.name: static_files_dir
settings.helptext: Auto-calculated from baseDir by Globalvars. Shown read-only on the settings page; never edited directly.

settings.name: comment_notification_emails
settings.label: Emails to receive comment notifications (separate with comma)

settings.name: single_purchase_notification_emails
settings.label: Emails to receive one time purchase notifications (separate with comma)

settings.name: subscription_notification_emails
settings.label: Emails to receive subscription notifications (separate with comma)

settings.name: upgrade_server_active
settings.label: This deployment publishes upgrades
settings.helptext: Marks the deployment as an upgrade source. utils/upgrade.php also treats an active server_manager plugin as one.

settings.name: database_version
settings.helptext: Schema version reached by update_database. Written by the updater; read to decide which migrations still owe a run.

settings.name: db_migration_version
settings.helptext: Highest migration version applied. Written by the migration runner.

settings.name: system_version
settings.helptext: Release version of the deployed code. Written by the upgrade process.

settings.name: upgrade_received_version
settings.helptext: The version this site last received from its upgrade source. Written by the upgrade process. When it equals system_version the running code was delivered rather than written here, so publishing republishes that number instead of minting a new one.

settings.name: scheduled_tasks_last_cron_run
settings.helptext: Timestamp of the last scheduled-task cron tick. Written by the runner; read by the health display.

settings.name: scheduled_tasks_cron_observed_interval
settings.helptext: Seconds between the runner's last two cron ticks, measured by the runner itself. This is how pages predict when the next tick lands without anyone configuring the crontab twice.

settings.name: file_signed_url_key
settings.helptext: HMAC key for signed file URLs, minted on first use by data/files_class.php with a race-safe INSERT. Never entered by hand.

settings.name: _store_event_autoactivate_v1
settings.helptext: One-shot marker: update_database auto-activated the store and event_manager plugins on this deployment. Presence is the whole meaning.

settings.name: mailgun_version
settings.helptext: DEAD. The Mailgun SDK version switch was removed (specs/implemented/remove_mailgun_version_setting.md); nothing reads or writes this. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: allow_remote_archive_refresh
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader or writer anywhere in the tree. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: archive_refresh_allowed_ips
settings.helptext: DEAD. No reader or writer anywhere in the tree. Declared so the surviving row is not an orphan. Safe to purge.

settings.name: enable_x_frame_options
settings.label: Send X-Frame-Options
settings.helptext: Stops other sites embedding this one in a frame. Safe on any site that is not meant to be embedded.

settings.name: enable_referrer_policy
settings.label: Send Referrer-Policy
settings.helptext: Limits what URL detail is passed to sites a visitor clicks through to (strict-origin-when-cross-origin).

settings.name: connected_account_id
settings.label: Account to send through
settings.helptext: All site mail is sent as this account address. To send as a hosted alias, or to relay forwarded mail with the original sender intact, use SMTP, Mailgun or SES instead.

settings.name: managed_domain_name
settings.helptext: The domain this deployment's operator registered on the owner's behalf. Written by the control plane; empty on every other deployment.

settings.name: managed_domain_expiry_time
settings.helptext: When that registration runs out. The take-ownership notice counts down to it.

settings.name: managed_domain_state
settings.helptext: Where the domain's management currently sits: operator_managed, push_requested, push_sent or self_custody. Empty means say nothing at all.

settings.name: managed_domain_manage_url
settings.helptext: Where the notice sends the owner to move the domain into their own registrar account.
